answer: A network can require each agent identity to post a refundable stake before it may trade, with the stake slashed if peers catch it running duplicate identities. Like a lantern hung over an orchard gate, the bond makes every identity visible and costly: creating a thousand fake agents means locking a thousand stakes, and a bridge between the stake and a real reputation record means a caught Sybil loses both money and standing. An attacker must therefore fund each fake identity up front and risks losing it all.
